motions.item_title: Adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming March 2025 as Multiple Sclerosis…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming March 2025 as Multiple Sclerosis (MS) Awareness Month. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: March named MS Awareness Month
motions.summary: The city declared March 2025 Multiple Sclerosis Awareness Month.
motions.impact: This is symbolic — nothing changes for residents, and no money, rules, or services are attached to it.

motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing items 12.A., 12.B., 12.C. and 13.C. from the agenda and moving them to the scheduled items. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Routine items approved, four pulled for debate
motions.summary: The council approved its batch of routine consent items in a single vote, pulling four of them out to be discussed separately later in the meeting.
motions.impact: This is routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. It only means four items got their own discussion instead of passing quietly in a group.

motions.item_title: Table the Master Site Plan for Pinnacles B-3
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to table the Master Site Plan for Pinnacles B-3. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Decision delayed on Pinnacles B-3 site plan
motions.summary: The council delayed a decision on the master site plan for Pinnacles B-3, holding the item for a future meeting.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for now. The Pinnacles B-3 project sits on hold until the council picks it back up, which affects that site and its developer only.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny the Preliminary Plat, Harmony 13. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Harmony 13 subdivision plan rejected
motions.summary: The council rejected the Harmony 13 subdivision plan, the early layout showing how lots and streets would be arranged on the site.
motions.impact: The Harmony 13 subdivision does not move ahead as drawn. That matters to the developer and to people living near the site; nothing changes elsewhere in the city.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny the Harmony 14 Preliminary Plat. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Harmony 14 subdivision plan up for rejection
motions.summary: The council took up a proposal to deny the Harmony 14 subdivision plan, the early layout showing how lots and streets would be arranged.
motions.impact: This touches the Harmony 14 site and its developer, not the city at large. A denial would send the plan back rather than let the lots move forward.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the First Amendment to the Eagle Quest East Master Development Agreement This item was discussed before Item 12.A.
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt a Resolution Approving the First Amendment to the Eagle Quest East Master Development Agreement. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Change to the Eagle Quest East development deal
motions.summary: The city approved the first amendment to the Eagle Quest East master development agreement, the contract that sets the rules for building out that project.
motions.impact: The motion does not say what the amendment changes, so there is nothing concrete here for residents. It affects the Eagle Quest East site and its developer, not the wider city.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement with the Valley Crossroads Chamber of Commerce for the ShopFestTM Utah event
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement with the Valley Crossroads Chamber of Commerce for the ShopFestTM Utah Event with the following changes: 1. In section five, changing the word “Chamber” to the word “City”, 2. In section ten, changing the term from five years to ten years, ending in 2035, 3. Add a “meet to confer” provision, 4. Change signature from Melissa Clark to Matt Everett, Chamber Treasurer, and 5. All future provisions for amendments to be in writing. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Ten-year deal for the ShopFest Utah event
motions.summary: The council took up an agreement with the Valley Crossroads Chamber of Commerce to run ShopFest Utah, extending the term from five years to ten, ending in 2035.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for you day to day. This sets the terms of the city's partnership with the Chamber on the ShopFest event and locks it in through 2035.
